aspects.says: Cipher.getInstance("AES") on SunJCE is AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding, which encrypts equal 16-byte blocks to equal ciphertext blocks and uses no IV.
basis: section:Cipher.getInstance("AES") Is ECB, and ECB Encrypts Equal Blocks to Equal Blocks

aspects.says: MessageDigest.isEqual gives the same answers as Arrays.equals, but its time depends only on the length of its first argument, while Arrays.equals returns at the first mismatch.
basis: section:Compare Tags and Hashes with MessageDigest.isEqual; Arrays.equals Stops at the First Difference

aspects.says: AES-GCM stores a 12-byte IV in front of the ciphertext and a 16-byte tag after it, and decryption throws AEADBadTagException for any changed byte; a mode without a tag, such as CTR, decrypts a changed ciphertext into changed plaintext.
basis: section:AES-GCM Refuses a Changed Ciphertext; Encryption Without a Tag Doesn't

aspects.says: Two GCM encryptions under the same key and IV share a keystream, so their ciphertexts XOR to the XOR of the plaintexts; each encryption needs its own IV, stored with the ciphertext.
basis: section:A GCM IV Used Twice Under One Key Gives Away the XOR of the Two Plaintexts

aspects.says: SunJCE refuses a repeated key and IV for GCM encryption only on the same Cipher object; a new Cipher accepts them.
basis: section:A GCM IV Used Twice Under One Key Gives Away the XOR of the Two Plaintexts

aspects.says: SunJCE's GCM decryption releases no plaintext from update(); all of it comes from doFinal after the tag matched.
basis: section:AES-GCM Refuses a Changed Ciphertext; Encryption Without a Tag Doesn't
aspects.reason: a property of the provider rather than of the reader's code; field-cipher grades the observable consequence, that a changed value never comes back as text

aspects.says: A password hash needs a random salt per user, so equal passwords differ, and an iteration count, stored with the hash, that makes each guess cost; PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 provides both and plain SHA-256 neither.
basis: section:A Password Hash Needs a Salt per User and a Slow Function: PBKDF2, Not SHA-256

aspects.says: A salt makes equal passwords look different but doesn't make a single guess slower; the iteration count does.
basis: section:A Password Hash Needs a Salt per User and a Slow Function: PBKDF2, Not SHA-256
